changes: p1 Uddhavarāja: role changed from 'owner' to 'author' (compiler). 'sañcitam idaṃ pustakaṃ' means he compiled the book at the NS 731 pratiṣṭhā, not that he owned it. Confidence lowered to medium.
Note added that p1 Uddhavarāja and p2 Uddhavanātha are probably the same person, Kālīdāsa's guru. They are kept as separate records.
Place stays empty: Caparitale (a sattal) is where the pratiṣṭhā was performed, not where the copy was made. The notes now say so.
Notes now give the CE date of the first date (NS 731, about 1610 CE).

persons.name: Uddhavarāja
persons.evidence: śrī upādhyā uddhavarājena sañcitam idaṃ pustakaṃ

date.as_written: saṃvat 746 caitra śukla navamyāntithau puṣyanakṣatre ādityavāsare

purpose: for the pleasure of the Goddess (śrīśrīśrīdevīprītir astu)
notes: The colophon gives two dates. Both are in NS and they do not conflict. (1) NS 731 kārttika kṛṣṇa 3, budhavāra, Rohiṇī nakṣatra (about 1610 CE): the day the Guhyakālīpratiṣṭhā was performed and a pratiṣṭhā held at the sattal of Caparitale. On that day Upādhyāya Uddhavarāja compiled (sañcitam) the book. This is probably the exemplar or the original compilation of the ritual manual. (2) NS 746 caitra śukla 9, Sunday, Puṣya nakṣatra (1626 CE): the date this copy was written by Kālīdāsa, through the grace of his guru Uddhavanātha. Uddhavarāja and Uddhavanātha are very likely the same person (Uddhava-), so the guru would be the compiler. They are not merged because the names differ. Another possible reading of 'sañcita' is 'collected/acquired', which would make p1 an owner of the exemplar. Caparitale is the place of the pratiṣṭhā; the place of copying is not stated.
